newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - GE reports record 1996 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - GE reports record 1996 earnings.

text.p: General Electric Co, in reporting record 1996 results, said it expected an even better 1997. The company issued the following text with its earnings results. The earnings table appeared separately.

FAIRFIELD, Conn., Jan. 16 /PRNewswire/ -- GE (NYSE: GE) achieved record revenues, earnings, operating margin and operating cash flow in 1996, Chairman John F. Welch reported today. "The year's double-digit increases again demonstrate the ability of GE's diverse mix of leading global businesses to deliver top-line growth, increased margins and strong cash generation," Mr. Welch said. Highlights of the Company's preliminary results include:

-- Earnings per share increased 13% to $4.40, up from last year's $3.90, and earnings increased 11% to a record $7.280 billion. Earnings per share grew faster than earnings, reflecting the impact of shares repurchased under a four-year, $13 billion share repurchase program initiated in December 1994.

-- Revenues, including acquisitions, rose to a record $79.2 billion. This 13% increase was driven primarily by GE Capital Services, increased global activities across GE, higher sales of spare parts and services by GE's equipment businesses and revenues from the Summer Olympic Games televised by NBC. Revenues increased at nine of GE's twelve businesses, led by double-digit growth at GE Capital Services, NBC and Power Systems.

-- GE's 1996 operating margin rate was 14.8% of sales, up from 14.4% in 1995, and was a record for the Company. Nine businesses, led by Power Systems, NBC, Appliances, Medical Systems and Aircraft Engines, reported higher operating margins.
-- Eleven of GE's twelve businesses reported higher operating profit for the year, with five GE Capital Services, Power Systems, NBC, Medical Systems and Motors achieving double-digit increases.
-- GE Capital Services' earnings for 1996 increased 17% to $2.817 billion.
The record results were led by strong double-digit
increases in all GE's activities, with particularly strong performance by Consumer Services and Specialty Insurance.

-- Cash generated from GE's operating activities in 1996 was a record $9.1 billion, up $3.0 billion from last year's $6.1 billion due to improvements in earnings and working capital. This continued strong cash generation helped lower GE's debt-to-capital ratio from 11.6% to 11.4%, even with $3.3 billion of share repurchases during the year. As part of the $13 billion share repurchase program, GE purchased $6.4 billion 94 million shares during the past 25 months. Return on equity improved to a record 24.0% from a comparable 23.5% in 1995.

-- Fourth-quarter earnings per share increased 13% to $1.26, up from last year's $1.12, and earnings increased 11% to $2.067 billion. GE's fourth-quarter earnings were its first quarterly results exceeding $2 billion and the highest of any quarter in the company's history.
Revenues in the fourth quarter were a company record $23.0 billion, 16% higher than last year's $19.8 billion.
At its December meeting, the GE Board of Directors increased the company's quarterly dividend by 13%, which marked the 21st consecutive year of increased dividends by GE.

The company's share repurchase program was increased from $9 billion to $13 billion and extended through 1998. The board also recommended a two-for-one stock split for approval at the April 23, 1997 annual share owners meeting.

"In addition to delivering record performance for the year, GE's businesses made aggressive moves in globalization, service, quality and new product introduction to position GE for future growth," Mr. Welch said.
Highlights of recent activities in these four areas included:

-- GE's globalization continued at a rapid pace in 1996 with revenues outside the U. S. again reflecting a double-digit increase to about $33 billion, more than 40% of GE's total revenues. During the year, GE's businesses took actions to broaden their global reach by making acquisitions in countries that included Germany, Japan, France, the United Kingdom, Italy, Brazil, Indonesia, India, Mexico and Australia.

-- Servicing of GE's installed base of equipment accelerated in 1996 with revenues increasing at a double digit rate to $8.4 billion. GE's equipment businesses received large multi-year service contracts from British Airways, USAir, Columbia/HCA and Burlington Northern Santa Fe.
Aircraft Engines broadened its service market presence

with acquisitions in Brazil, Malaysia and the Philippines. GE and Harris Corp formed another joint venture beyond their railroad electronics company to provide energy management solutions to the power generation market.

-- GE invested $200 million in 1996 to launch the Six Sigma quality initiative across all GE businesses. Thousands of GE employees received Six Sigma training for improving product and process quality, led by 1,800 new "black belt" quality leaders. The yield from the first year of the Six Sigma program came close to paying for the investment. In 1997, GE will increase its Six Sigma quality investment to $300 million and expects $400-$500 million in savings from this initiative resulting in $100-$200 million in operating margin improvements.

-- The introduction of new products and services was a thrust of every GE business. NBC launched MSNBC, a 24-hour news and information service currently distributed to 28 million subscribers. GE Capital continued its expansion into the insurance and annuity product market by acquiring both First Colony and Life of Virginia; it also expanded in the fast-growing computer servicing market with acquisitions of AmeriData and CompuNet. Aircraft Engines continued its strong market position by winning more than 60% of orders for large commercial engines in 1996 and received ETOPS (extended range twin-engine operation) approval from the FAA for the GE90-powered Boeing 777. Medical Systems' new ultrasound products grew 25% in a relatively flat global market. GE's new home laundry appliance line was received very positively by U.S. consumers and made dramatic gains in market share which helped to drive appliance earnings growth and operating margin gains in a very competitive global market.

Mr. Welch concluded, "GE's 239,000 employees around the world are extremely proud of their precedent-setting performance in 1996 and are confident that GE enters 1997 better positioned than ever to deliver another year of record results to our share owners."
